az_willow_pinnacle.blurb: A compact sport crag on Mount Lemmon in the Santa Catalina Mountains, part of the mid-mountain Willow Canyon Crags group. All five routes sit in the 5.11 to 5.12 range, with three at 5.11 and two at 5.12, so it suits strong climbers more than newcomers. The face is short but steep, built around a slightly overhanging prow, and it stands directly beside the trail. Getting there takes roughly 35 minutes on foot, walking beyond two other crags on the way in.

az_sycamore_wall.blurb: A granite wall of roughly 150 to 200 feet in Central Arizona, just south of Sunflower and visible from the Beeline Highway on the east side of the road. All five routes are traditional lines, running from 5.8 up to 5.10, with most at 5.9 and 5.10. The hike to the base is steep and goes up a canyon, though the scenery along the way is described as making the effort worthwhile.

az_chitty_chitty_bang_bang.blurb: A small trad crag within Stewart Pocket, the granite climbing zone near Payson in Central Arizona. The rock is a dome whose face looks north. Five routes cover easy to moderate ground: one around 5.6, three at 5.8 and one at 5.9. It lies south of the main trail that runs between Stewart Peak and Ashley's Block, so you can spot it while walking in, and it shares its approach with those neighbouring formations.
